data.content: The run confirms the problem is confined to generated API labels plus prose blocks that are pure code, URLs, or identifiers. I’m checking the segment classifier now; the key hypothesis is that these are tagged as translatable text before the existing verbatim policy gets a chance to preserve them.

The diagnosis holds: `translateUnits` only treats verbatim strings as cacheable when a caller supplies them, but the API pipeline supplies none. As a result, identifier-only sidebar labels and code-only prose are sent to the model, rejected as source-identical, and retried forever. I’ll add an API-specific classifier that copies those units verbatim into the PO cache, with tests for identifiers, URLs, CSS declarations, and ordinary prose.

I’m making this at the API pipeline boundary, not in the generic memory: it will preserve only API-shaped technical units, while ordinary UI labels and prose remain eligible for Hungarian translation. The cheap check is the existing mocked API-build test, extended to prove those units bypass the adapter and are written as source text.

data.content: The guide pipeline takes the opposite approach: whole guide files are catalogued first, then translated as Markdown, with technical content masked inside the adapter rather than classified before cache lookup. data.content:
`docs:guides` doesn’t have an equivalent classifier. It treats each guide as one whole-file PO entry with `translate: "always"` in [tools/i18n-engine/src/pipeline.ts](tools/i18n-engine/src/pipeline.ts), then [docs/scripts/translate-guide-po.ts](docs/scripts/translate-guide-po.ts) sends the file through `AiTranslationAdapter.translateMarkdown()`.

That adapter protects fenced code, inline code, `@scope/package` names, and escaped generic brackets before prompting the model. It asks the model to preserve URLs, import paths, and identifiers, then restores protected blocks afterward. Prompt-fence bodies are translated separately.

The API pipeline is different because it extracts thousands of small prose/label units. A unit that is only `AggregateOptions` or `cursor: auto.` reaches the model alone, comes back unchanged, and the passthrough guard rejects it from the cache. That is why it needs a pre-cache “required verbatim” classifier.

So your instinct is right: the API helper is terse because it encodes only the small-unit cases that the guide pipeline avoids by translating whole Markdown documents. The shared part worth extracting would be the technical-fragment detection/masking policy; the guide implementation itself does not currently provide a reusable “never translate” list.
